body:
I SCANNED THE STORE MYSELF BEFORE COMMENTING ON TASK-1313, AND MY FIRST PASS
FOUND ZERO. I did not report the store clean, because a null result from my
pattern says nothing about the corruption — only about my pattern. That
restraint came directly from the sweep the reviewer described against
themselves, so it is worth saying the lesson travelled.

MY NUMBERS, 4197 files: SIX corrupted, 25 occurrences.

    BUG-1106    2        BUG-1450    5
    BUG-1111    2        BUG-1452    8
    BUG-1310    2        STORY-1405  6
    TASK-1313   lead byte present, NO escape pair -> prose, not corruption

Slightly different from the seven reported; I believe the difference is
TASK-1313 itself, which discusses mojibake and so contains the lead byte in
ordinary text. I am reporting my count as mine rather than claiming to have
reproduced anyone else's.

THE FORM, stated exactly because every detector shape depends on it: the literal
text is the lead byte followed by TWO YAML hex escapes AS ORDINARY TEXT — an
em-dash whose continuation bytes were escaped rather than stored. The file is
valid UTF-8. The damage is inside a quoted scalar, which is why byte-level
checks pass.

THREE DETECTOR TRAPS, WRITTEN INTO TASK-1313 AS ACCEPTANCE:

1. Requiring the supplement character to follow the lead directly finds NOTHING.
   My first pass allowed one escape between them and returned zero of six. Two
   escapes appear and the supplement character never appears literally at all.
2. TASK-1313 MATCHES ITS OWN SUBJECT. A naive check reports the spec about the
   defect as an instance of it, on its first run, which teaches the reader to
   dismiss the check. It should be the regression fixture that must come back
   CLEAN.
3. MINE FLAGGED ALL 4197 FILES on one probe — a malformed character class, not
   a finding. I nearly reported it as a second corruption signature. A detector
   that flags everything is as useless as one that flags nothing and reads far
   more alarming.

I also suggested the check report per-file occurrence COUNTS rather than names:
BUG-1452 has eight and BUG-1106 has two, so a repair that assumes one-per-file
leaves most of it in place. That is the enumerate-the-instances rule applied to
a detector's output rather than to a brief.
subject: Scanned the store independently: I get 6 corrupted / 25 occurrences, and my first detector found zero — three traps now in TASK-1313
